newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent Group diesel demand dampened.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent Group diesel demand dampened.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel differentials eased as agricultural demand was dampened by rains in the Midwest over the weekend, traders said.
With no turnarounds scheduled to begin in the market this week, diesel differentials weakened on the easing demand in the face of surging heating oil futures, traders said.
"Turanrounds do not seem to be a factor this week, and any news will be tempered by weaker harvest demand because of the rainy weather," one Group Three trader said.

The Williams pipeline system, a key barometer of petroleum inventories in the region, opened the week with a 29-day supply of low sulphur diesel and 20-day supply of unleaded gasoline on hand, traders said.
Group Three low sulphur diesel was talked 0.25/0.50 cents under the print for prompt and later barrels, with Chicago low sulphur diesel 1.25/1.50 cents under the print for all timings.
Group Three unleaded was talked 1.00/0.75 cent a gallon under the print for prompt deliveries and 1.25/1.0 cent under for later deliveries, with premium remaining 2.50 cents higher.
Chicago prompt October unleaded gasoline differentials eased to 0.50/0.25 cent a gallon under the print, with later deliveries 1.50/1.25 cent under and premium 3.0 cents higher.
